note: Placed pieces (docs 09, docs/future/10; src/world/pieces): objects that rest on the ground rather than being part of it. The first is the loose stone, the naturalist's reward at six finds (naturalist.json). cap: how many loose stones an island may hold; at the cap the Loose stone mode says so calmly and sets no more. sizeM: a stone's length in meters [min, max], picked by its seed. sink: the share of a stone's height set into the ground, so it sits rather than rests. lean: how much of the ground's slope a stone leans with (0 level, 1 flat on the slope). grassClear: blades stand no nearer a stone's middle than this share of its half length (src/render/passes/grass.js clears), so it sits in the grass rather than the grass growing through it. tapM and tapPerM: how near a tap must be to pick a stone (plus this much per meter of camera distance; never less than about half the stone's length). arrive: when the reward is given, count stones come by themselves on grounds (painted grass or soil) between nearM [min, max] meters from fresh water (a pond or stream, never the sea or a damp hollow), never in water, on ground no steeper than maxSlope (rise over run across a meter), at least spacingM apart; placed from the world seed, so live play and catch-up give the same stones. tip: a tap on a stone lifts its near edge by tipDeg over tipS seconds (pivoting on the far edge, so you see underneath), holds for holdS, then settles back over settleS. shape: the stones are baked from blended ellipsoids (src/world/creatures/body-bake.js): count shapes, seeded from seed; widthShare and heightShare [min, max] of the length; lobes extra lumps blended in by blendM; cellM the bake grid; then cut by facets: a top plane tilted up to topTilt and cutting at topShare [min, max] of the stone's reach upward (a flatter top), and chips planes round the shoulders, rising chipUp [min, max] and cutting at chipShare of the reach that way. albedo: weathered grey stone (linear, darker than fresh rock, in the island rock's own hue); underside: damp and soil-stained where it lies in the ground; mottle: broad and fine tone wander (shares) at broadPerUnit and finePerUnit waves per mesh unit, and hue a touch warmer or cooler with the broad patches. The draw pass (src/shaders/piece-draw.wgsl) lays the island's scanned rock over this, triplanar in the stone's frame: its variation about the rock's mean (terrain.json albedoRock), its normals (look.normalStrength) and roughness. Albedos are physical; the palette paints at tonemap (docs/05). damp: the dark patch the stone leaves on the ground, as a share of its footprint (scale), with its albedo at the middle and edge (linear). ring: the soft damp darkening of the ground round each stone's foot: darkness 0..1, scale over the footprint. words: the Loose stone mode's calm lines (full at the cap, water when a tap lands in water).

words.full: The island holds all the loose stones it can for now. Remove one to set it somewhere else.
words.water: A loose stone sits on land. Tap the ground.

driftwoodNote: Driftwood (docs 13, docs/future/10; src/world/pieces/driftwood.js), the naturalist's reward at ten finds. Once given, each high tide may leave logs on its strandline (shore.json look.strandline): only the newest lines keep logs (lines), each tide perTide [min, max] logs, at most most on the island at once; a log lies on dry or damp ground within bandReachM of the sea's tide band (never a pond's bank), where the ground is within lineToleranceM of the line's reach and both its ends within endToleranceM, on ground no steeper than maxSlope, along the shore give or take yawJitterDeg, at least spacingM apart. Seeded from the world seed and the tide, so nothing is saved: a later tide that sweeps the line takes its logs. lengthM and thickM [min, max]: a log's size in meters. sink: the share of its thickness set into the sand; lean: how much of the slope it leans with. grassClear: blades stand no nearer than its half thickness plus grassClearM, in circles along its length. tapReachM: a tap picks a log within its half thickness and this much of its line (a tap on a low log's top lands on the sand behind it). ringHalf: the damp ring's half width and half length as shares of its footprint. roll: a tap rolls it rollDeg away from you over tipS, holds holdS, and rolls back over settleS, showing the damp sand where it lay (damp: that patch's albedos, linear). shape: count log shapes seeded from seed, each around vertices round and rings along; bow and taper [min, max] (shares of its thickness and its radius), swell a gentle unevenness, knots [min, max] of knotSize [min, max] (shares of its length) rising knotRise; jag how far the broken ends are torn back (share of its length). albedo: sea-weathered silver-grey (linear), endAlbedo the end grain, knotAlbedo round the knots, underside where it lies in the damp sand below stainLine (a share of its thickness); mottle: broad and fine tone along its length. look (piece-draw.wgsl): roughness, bumpM the grain and cracks' relief, grainAcross streaks across the log, crackDarkness 0..1. cap: how many logs an island keeps (apart from the stones' cap). carry: the turtles' gift (unlocks.carry, or ?sandbox, or ?driftwood): a carried piece hangs liftM above its spot until set down.
steppingNote: Stepping stones and the treads of Steps (docs 09; src/world/pieces/slabs.js): each is one of a small library of rounded slab shapes, 1 mesh unit long, that the draw pass scales and turns. slab: count shapes, seeded from seed, each around vertices round, with topRings rings across its top and bevelRows rows round its rounded edge. The footprint is a rounded rectangle (a superellipse): widthShare [min, max] is its width as a share of its length, power [min, max] how square its corners are (2 an oval, higher squarer), and its outline wobbles by wobble (a share) in wobbleHarmonics [min, max] gentle waves round it. The top is nearly flat: domeShare [min, max] how much it rises in the middle (share of the length), tiltDeg [min, max] how far it leans; bevelShare [min, max] the radius of the rounded edge; capShare [min, max] how thick the stone looks (how far below the top the sides turn straight down), the sides widening by batterShare over that depth and lumpy by lump (a share). skirtUnits: how far the sides go on down below that (in lengths), so a stone can stand on a deep pond bed; the draw pass sinks what is not needed into the ground. albedo: weathered grey stone (linear); underside: the stained tone the sides reach more than stainUnits (in lengths) below the top's lowest edge; topLift: how much lighter the top is, topSmooth how much of the fine grain it loses; mottle: broad and fine tone wander (shares) at broadPerUnit and finePerUnit waves per mesh unit, and hue a touch warmer or cooler with the broad patches. Albedos are physical; the palette paints at tonemap (docs/05).

words.full: The island holds all the pond stones it can for now. Remove some to lay them somewhere else.
words.deep: The water is too deep here for a stone to stand. Try nearer the edge.
words.hint: Drag across shallow water to lay a line of stones, or tap for one. Tap a stone to select it.

stepsNote: Steps (doc 13, the shaper's trail; src/world/pieces/steps.js): a flight cut between two levels of ground, dragged from one to the other. widthM: how wide a flight is (wide enough that the walker's half-metre grid always finds a level way up its middle). Every rise is at most maxRiseM and every tread at least minTreadM and at most maxTreadM, and the whole flight rises no steeper than maxPitch (rise over run), so the walker can always climb it; a drag shorter than that asks for more. minDropM: the least difference in level worth a step. landM: how far the flight runs on past each end at that end's level, so it meets the ground. cap: how many flights an island holds. rockShare: how far toward rock the flight's cells and the sheer walls beside it (any drop over faceDropM to a neighbour) are painted. slab: perTread slabs side by side on each tread, filling fill of their share (the rest is the gaps between them), turned up to yawJitterDeg off square, their tops riseM over the tread. words: the Steps mode's calm lines.

words.hint: Drag from a terrace down to the ground below to cut a flight of steps. Tap a flight to select it.
words.flat: These two places are at the same level. Start on a terrace and drag down to the ground below it.
words.short: That is too steep for steps. Drag a little further, about {m} m in all.
words.overlap: Steps are already cut here. Remove them first to cut new ones.
words.full: The island holds all the flights of steps it can for now.
words.water: Steps start and end on dry ground.
